params.body:
## What was wrong

The Studio has an optional SEO block on Home, About, cases and blog posts, and Home already holds a Dutch and an English meta title and description in it. Since the redesign's content layer, the site reads none of it:

- Home showed `We make your idea tangible | Cides` in both languages, with no "product design", "productontwikkeling" or "Brugge" in the title.
- All 82 pages shared `og-default.png` as their share image, cases with good hero photos included.
- The organisation JSON-LD lost `sameAs` (the three profile links in siteSettings), because `socialLinks` was hard-coded to an empty list.
- 42 of 82 meta descriptions ran past 160 characters (sector intros up to 337, the Sen case 529), so search results cut them mid-word.

## What changes

- `web/src/lib/seo.ts`
  - `resolveMeta`: an override counts only in the page's own language; otherwise the page default stays. A Dutch title on the English page would be the wrong language in the English result.
  - `metaDescription`: automatic descriptions keep whole sentences up to 160 characters, else cut at a word with an ellipsis. Editor overrides are used as written.
- Cases and posts share a 1200x630 JPG crop of their hero or cover (hotspot respected), unless the Studio sets a share image.
- `siteSettings.socialLinks` feeds `sameAs` again.

Result on a local build from production: Home becomes `Product design bureau voor innovatieve bedrijven | Cides` (NL) and `Product design agency for manufacturers | Cides` (EN), with the Studio descriptions that name Brugge/Bruges.

## Checked

- `npm test --workspace web`: 53 passed. The new tests fail when the language rule or the length cap is broken.
- `npx astro check`: 0 errors.
- Local production build: same 82 sitemap URLs, the same 5 noindex pages (404 and empty blog categories), share image URL returns 200 image/jpeg.
- The built `<body>` of Home, a case, About and a post is byte-identical to the live pages: only the head changes. No CSS touched.
params.title: Read the Studio SEO overrides again and fit meta descriptions
